title: the Marlowe Estate Rising Revisited
premise: Ines Sandoval, the cathedral's archivist, is paid a suspiciously generous retainer by a stranger who insists that a murder at the decaying Marlowe Estate will occur within a fortnight — and wants Ines to prove it never happens. When the predicted victim dies exactly on schedule, Ines realizes the client isn't preventing murder but scripting an alibi, and that the killer has been feeding on the estate's sealed records and the crypt below the cathedral. Using their talent for reading what documents conceal rather than reveal, Ines lays a false trail through forged archives to trap the killer mid-ritual in the locked crypt. The murderer — the estate's own historian, erasing witnesses to an old inheritance crime — is caught, but only after Ines must confront a memory of their own that the killer had weaponized against them.
about_author: Tamsin Nakamura is a former parish registrar who spent a decade cataloguing ecclesiastical archives across three countries before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who believe paper remembers what flesh prefers to forget.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A well-dressed stranger arrives at the cathedral archive with cash in advance: prove that no murder occurs at Marlowe Estate on the fourteenth of the month. Ines, who has quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths, accepts out of professional offense at being hired for a non-crime. The beat is wary curiosity — the reader senses the trap closing before Ines does.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Forgot
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Researching the Marlowe Estate's deeds, Ines finds pages razored from the parish ledger — precisely where a 1970s death was recorded. A visit to the crumbling estate reveals a family obsessed with its own curated history. The emotional beat is the thrill of the hunt curdling into unease as Ines realizes someone else has been editing this story for decades.

chapters.title: The Fourteenth
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On the appointed day, Ines stakes out the estate; nothing happens — until the estate's elderly groundskeeper is found drowned in the flooded boathouse, ruled accidental. The date matched. The client calls, satisfied: proof delivered, payment doubled. Ines feels cold horror instead of triumph, understanding they were hired to certify a murder, not prevent one.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with a flashback thread. Revisiting the three deaths Ines previously unraveled, Ines maps them onto the Marlowe timeline and finds each victim connected to the estate's missing ledger years. Detective Okafor, who once dismissed Ines as a crank, grudgingly listens. The beat is alliance-building and dread: the killer isn't improvising; they're completing a list.

chapters.title: The Historian's Hand
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Suspicion falls on Edmund Vane, the estate's archivist-historian, whose handwriting matches marginalia in the mutilated ledger. But when Ines confronts him, Vane produces documents proving he was abroad during the drowning — documents Ines recognizes as forgeries, because they imitate her own archival style too well. The beat is vertigo: the killer knows her methods intimately.

chapters.title: A Memory With Teeth
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, intimate and destabilizing. Anonymous letters arrive quoting details from Ines's childhood in the cathedral orphanage — things recorded nowhere except a file Ines herself sealed twenty years ago. The killer has read her own past like she reads others'. The emotional beat is fear turning inward; the hunter realizes she is also quarry.

chapters.title: Below the Locked Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the letters' references, Ines breaks into the cathedral's locked crypt and finds a workspace: copies of every case file, photographs of the victims, and a half-finished dossier on the next name — Detective Okafor's. The beat is grim resolve. Ines stops investigating and starts planning, deciding to feed the killer a fabricated archive.

chapters.title: The Forged Trail
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with brief interludes from the killer's perspective, unnamed. Ines plants a convincing fake record implicating Vane in the 1970s death, knowing the killer cannot resist correcting a flawed archive. The killer takes the bait, requesting access to verify the forgery. The beat is cat-and-mouse tension, two archivists lying to each other in ink.

chapters.title: Crypt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ines and the killer — revealed as the cathedral's beloved sub-sacristan, who grew up alongside Ines in the orphanage and discovered the Marlowe cover-up in the same sealed files. Confronted among the tombs, he argues the murders are justice; Ines answers with the truth of his first victim, an innocent. Okafor arrives as the trap closes. The beat is grief braided with fury.

chapters.title: Rebinding
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Weeks later, Ines restores the mutilated ledger, reconstructing the stolen names from memory and testimony — including her own. The client vanishes, revealed as the last Marlowe heir who wanted the murders certified, not solved, and is arrested. Ines reopens the crypt to the light. The final beat is quiet restoration: memory, honestly kept, as both wound and cure.
